## TL;DR

The overlay mutation observer inspected queued DOM nodes with `node instanceof Element`. That expression depends on the jsdom realm's global `Element` being present when the observer callback runs. A queued MutationObserver delivery can arrive during worker teardown, after that realm global has been removed, producing the reported `ReferenceError`. The check now identifies element nodes by `nodeType === 1` and only then uses the element methods needed to find overlay layers. This keeps the behavior and avoids a global stub.

## Work and rationale

I traced the candidate error to `src/ui-app/src/lib/activity-motion.ts`, specifically `nodeTouchesOverlayLayer`. The helper is called for added and removed nodes in the singleton overlay DOM observer. The observer is disconnected when its final listener detaches and from the test reset helper, but `disconnect()` cannot make code that is already queued safe if that code still references a torn-down realm global.

The change replaces the realm-sensitive `instanceof Element` test with the DOM node type check. Node type 1 is the platform's element-node discriminator. After the check, the node is cast to `Element` so the existing `hasAttribute` and `querySelector` checks remain unchanged. This addresses the specific realm-global dependency implicated by the error without changing observer lifetime, adding timeout behavior, or stubbing globals.

I searched the available `.repoos` tree for the historical stack traces requested in the task notes, but this worktree contains no agent logs or review logs with those entries. The task description identifies the coordinator and overlay observer as the likely source; the code path above matches the reported failure signature.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the activity motion coordinator and its tests, including unmount cleanup and the shared observer reset path. The observer has explicit disconnect logic both when its listener reference count reaches zero and in `resetActivityMotionCoordinatorForTests`. The callback still had a global `Element` lookup, which can fail independently of disconnect once delivery has been queued.

The first whole UI-app run was attempted before build artifacts existed and had 11 unrelated failures across 4 files. After `repoos check` built the worktree, I ran the complete UI-app suite twice. Both runs passed all 709 test files, with 9,479 tests passing and 9 skipped each time. Neither run reported `Element is not defined`. These post-change runs show stable passing behavior; because the baseline failure was intermittent and did not reproduce in this session before the fix, they are not a controlled before/after reproduction.

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. It ran changed-path validation remotely, including build and the 110-file UI test selection (1,183 tests), plus the local format, lint, build, contrast audit and UI smoke gates. The suite completed before the report was finalized.

## Challenges and blockers

The historical run logs mentioned by the task were not present in the worktree, so I could not verify the exact originating test or observer callback. The first full suite run also happened before build artifacts existed and failed in unrelated artifact-dependent tests; after the required check built the worktree, two full runs passed. The focused observer behavior was not independently reproduced as a failure before the change.

## Key learnings

Disconnecting a MutationObserver is necessary lifecycle cleanup, but callback code should also be safe when its environment is changing. A callback that consults a global constructor with `instanceof` can throw if the DOM realm is being torn down. Checking the DOM node type avoids that dependency while retaining the same element-only behavior.
